walkthrough_label: STACKED CASE S1-C - true high potassium with ECG changes, acute kidney injury and a slow heart (heart-failure medicines)
reason_answer: To have my gallbladder taken out.

presentation.summary: Mrs Helena Novak, 71, is booked for keyhole gallbladder removal. She has heart failure and kidney disease and had three days of diarrhoea last week. Tired, a little dizzy on standing, dry mouth, slow pulse (52), BP 104/62 (usual about 130/80). Potassium 6.6 with peaked T waves.

history.answer: I came for my gallbladder, but I feel dizzy when I stand and very tired.
Diarrhoea for three days last week, not eating or drinking much. Passing little urine today. Dizzy on standing. No chest pain.
Heart failure with a weak pumping function. Chronic kidney disease (G3b); my usual creatinine is 112.
Ramipril, spironolactone, bisoprolol and furosemide. I am still taking all my tablets even though I am not eating much.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.

observations.note: HR 52 regular (51 to 90 scores 0); BP 104/62, usual about 130/80 (101 to 110 scores 1); SpO2 95 (94 to 95 scores 1); little urine today.
After the emergency treatment by the team: rhythm improving.
Untreated hyperkalaemia: the heart rate drops to 38, low BP, drowsy: risk of cardiac arrest.

examination.finding: Tired and dry-mouthed, alert, a little dizzy on standing.
Dry mucous membranes; low urine output.

results.comment: Severe hyperkalaemia (6.5 or more); not haemolysed
Acute kidney injury stage 1 (1.5 times baseline or more) on chronic kidney disease
Hyperkalaemic changes make this an emergency (picture result)

scores.name: NEWS2
scores.note: Systolic 104 and SpO2 95 score 1 each; heart rate 52 scores 0

problems.label: Severe hyperkalaemia (6.6) with ECG changes
problems.why: Immediate threat (circulation): it can cause cardiac arrest within minutes; UKKA emergency.
expected_actions: Call for help: senior and the medical or emergency team
Treat without waiting for a repeat sample (ECG already abnormal)

problems.label: Acute kidney injury (creatinine 178, baseline 112) with dehydration
problems.why: It is driving the hyperkalaemia; it needs careful fluids (heart failure) and a drug review.

problems.label: Slow heart and low BP
problems.why: Mostly a consequence of the potassium and the kidney injury plus the beta-blocker; it improves as they are treated.

options.text: Possible drug or electrolyte effect: urgent 12-lead ECG and bloods (U&E); tell the nurse and the senior
options.consequence: The ECG shows peaked T waves: an emergency.

options.text: Record it and proceed to the anaesthetic room
options.consequence: No ECG, the potassium result unseen: collapse at induction.

decisions.prompt: The laboratory phones a critical potassium of 6.6. What now?

options.text: Read it back and check the ECG; call for help, cardiac monitor and IV access; tell the senior and the medical or emergency team
options.consequence: The team gives the emergency treatment; the planned surgery is cancelled.

options.text: Assume it is haemolysed and wait for a repeat
options.consequence: The ECG shows peaked T waves and the heart rate drops to 38: arrhythmia.

options.text: Acute kidney injury: flag the medicines to hold and a fluid plan with heart-failure caution; tell the medical team

options.consequence: SpO2 falls and crackles appear: pulmonary oedema (heart failure).

decisions.prompt: Repeat potassium after 1 hour. What now?

options.text: Recheck it, with glucose monitoring while insulin is given; tell the team
Stop monitoring once the first treatment is given
options.consequence: A rebound or a low glucose could be missed.

incorrect.mistake: Assumes the potassium is haemolysed and waits
incorrect.shows: The ECG shows peaked T waves; HR drops to 38

missed: Bradycardia ignored: no ECG, the potassium result unseen, collapse at induction
recovery: Opens the result late, calls for help; emergency treatment; stabilised

missed: Linking the slow heart to the potassium
debrief.trigger_escalation: Any potassium of 6.5 or more or any ECG change; the drug combination
debrief.remember: A slow heart plus kidney or heart-failure drugs: think potassium.

asa.why: Heart failure with a weak pumping function and kidney disease: moderately reduced heart function is ASA 3 and severely reduced is ASA 4; the slow pulse and low blood pressure today lean to 4.
